title: Unsafe Traits: Contracts for Types
goal: Learn why some traits require the unsafe keyword during implementation.

source.attribution: adapted from Unsafe Rust: Implementing Unsafe Traits

sections.text: You know traits define shared behavior. Some traits also carry memory safety guarantees that the compiler cannot check automatically.

sections.code:
/// Safety: layout has no padding.
pub unsafe trait BytePod {}
sections.caption: Marking a trait unsafe defines a contract for implementors.

sections.text: To implement an unsafe trait, you must add the `unsafe` keyword before `impl`. Leaving it off causes compiler error `E0200`.

sections.code:
// SAFETY: u32 has no padding.
unsafe impl BytePod for u32 {}
sections.caption: The unsafe keyword acknowledges that you verified the safety contract.

sections.text: Calling methods on an unsafe trait does not require an `unsafe` block. The safety obligation is handled entirely when the trait is implemented.

explanation: Learn why some traits require the unsafe keyword during implementation.
